title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & per-route cost breakdown
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Veridion Health through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Discussion covered tagging routes, token-level cost attribution, retention windows, and hosted vs dedicated economics. Customer requested security docs, an initial pilot plan (100k monthly requests), and a benchmark of their inference patterns. Next steps: send pricing + security pack, share sample dashboard and benchmark spreadsheet, schedule pilot kickoff for 4/20.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jordan from redwood, i'll hand off to priya for the console deep dive in a minute.
00:10 Marta Ruiz: great thanks, um we just want to see cost per route basically and how we can track models per endpoint, mostly for our patient-summary use case.
00:20 Priya Shah: great, i'll share my screen — tell me if the deck comes through. so this is the Redwood Console, top-level usage analytics, you can see token volume, latencies, error rates across models, and then drill into per-route dashboards.
00:43 Evan Cho: quick question, can you attribute cost down to a named route? we have multiple microservices calling same model.
00:49 Priya Shah: yes, that's the per-route breakdown — we ingest route metadata from requests and you can tag via SDK or header, the console will show tokens, compute time, and unit cost per route. pricing note: hosted is per-token, dedicated is reserved capacity so the unit economics shift. (mild laugh)
01:08 Marta Ruiz: when you say unit cost per route, how do you handle shared KV cache / prefix caching effects? some routes reuse prefixes heavily.
01:20 Priya Shah: good call — the console reports both raw token accounting and effective cost after cache credits. we surface cache hit rates and estimate cost avoided. for example you'll see cache hits reduce billed tokens for the route, and we show an adjusted cost line.
01:39 Laura Kim: do you keep raw transcripts? retention? we have strict patient data rules.
01:44 Jordan Blake: we don't store customer prompts by default in hosted unless you opt in, and for Private you control retention. we'll send SOC 2 + data residency docs after.
01:55 Evan Cho: and KMS? HSM?
02:00 Priya Shah: we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments, HSM options for enterprise, and you can set audit log retention windows per deployment.
02:12 Marta Ruiz: ok show the per-route view please.
02:15 Priya Shah: sure, drilling into a route — top panel shows tokens, latency p95, model version, and a waterfall cost breakdown: model compute, storage (kv cache), network. you can filter by model variant, timeframe, and apply cohorting tags (env, team).
02:37 Speaker 2: (mumble) the timeline you can pin for a canary deployment as well?
02:42 Priya Shah: yes you can pin a rollout and compare traffic between variants, console overlays deviation in latency and cost. we also surface quality regressions tied to evals.
02:55 Marta Ruiz: we're curious about geographical routing — some calls from EU need to stay in-region. how does cost change?
03:02 Priya Shah: region matters; the console annotates regional cost and latency, and our routing policies can send requests to region-specific pools. cost preview shows cross-region egress, and dedicated pools can be region-isolated.
03:18 Evan Cho: can we export the data to our BI? we want to join with SRE metrics.
03:22 Priya Shah: yes CSV/JSON exports and a metrics API, plus tracer hooks. we'll also share a sample benchmark spreadsheet (i'll drop link after).
03:31 Jordan Blake: quick note on tagging best practices — use route-level tags, model-version tags, and business-unit tags so cost maps cleanly to teams.
03:39 Marta Ruiz: walk me through an example, like patient-summary route that calls embeddings then generation.
03:45 Priya Shah: right — console will show two sub-routes or chained calls: embeddings ingestion and text-generation. embeddings cost is per-vector unit, generation is per-token; we show combined cost and allow you to break out by step. if you run batching/caching the effective per-request cost will drop and we highlight that.
04:10 Evan Cho: do you simulate batching savings in the console?
04:14 Priya Shah: we have a model that estimates savings given your qps and latency SLO; console suggests batching configs and quantization profiles in Optimize.
04:25 Marta Ruiz: hmm our SLO is 500ms p95 for patient-summary, so we can't batch aggressively. can you show a scenario with low latency and caching?
04:33 Priya Shah: yes, you can tune to favor latency — the console shows projected cost with different knobs: batch size, cache TTL, and quantization. (pause) let's open a hypothetical — here is an overlay comparing default vs optimized. you can see cost down 28% while p95 stays within 500ms.
05:02 Laura Kim: procurement question — how do you handle audits? do you provide CSV of all requests?
05:08 Jordan Blake: we provide audit logs for Private and Dedicated with immutable export; hosted customers get configurable retention windows and exports for compliance. we'll include audit-sample in the security pack.
05:20 Evan Cho: what about multi-tenant visibility? we need RBAC.
05:24 Priya Shah: console has RBAC, SSO/SAML integration, fine-grained project roles. you can restrict access to cost dashboards by role.
05:31 Marta Ruiz: any competitors mentioned in your benchmarking?
05:34 Jordan Blake: customers often compare us to big managed endpoints and some open-source runtimes; we'll share a short competitive note.
05:42 Priya Ruiz (sic): sorry i mean marta: for pilot sizing we estimated 100k monthly requests for the initial scope?
05:48 Marta Ruiz: yes that's ballpark.
05:50 Priya Shah: great, we recommend a 4-week pilot with dedicated hours to run your traces through our profiler; we can run a benchmark with your representative traffic and show per-route cost delta.
06:07 Evan Cho: how invasive is the profiler? can we run it in staging only?
06:11 Priya Shah: absolutely staging only; tracer hooks are sidecar or middleware-level, minimal latency and no request payload storage unless you opt in.
06:20 Jordan Blake: i'm going to show the cost breakdown screen — this one breaks cost into compute, egress, and storage. notice the per-route attribution column and the ability to reassign overhead to owning teams.
06:38 Evan Cho: sometimes infra costs (egress) are tricky to attribute — can we apply custom allocation rules?
06:43 Priya Shah: yes you can create allocation rules (percent-based or regex on routes) and apply them to dashboards.
06:50 Marta Ruiz: show the alerting and anomaly detection for cost spikes.
06:54 Priya Shah: here — we have baseline anomaly detection, you can set thresholds by route or model and trigger PagerDuty/Slack. it also surfaces sudden regressions after rollouts.
07:10 Laura Kim: procurement again — what's the price for the pilot? any credits?
07:14 Jordan Blake: we'll include a pilot credit; i'll follow up with exact pricing tiers.
07:18 Marta Ruiz: we have regulatory folks who will want a private deployment or VPC, is that typical?
07:23 Jordan Blake: many health customers opt for Private with customer-managed VPC and KMS; we can do hybrid where control plane is private and compute in your region.
07:33 Evan Cho: performance: you said your runtime supports kernel selection and continuous batching — can you share CPU/GPU profiles you recommend?
07:42 Priya Shah: yes, for gen models we recommend A100 equivalent or higher for low p95; console shows recommended clouds and quantization profiles per model.
07:52 Marta Ruiz: do you support BYO-models? we have a fine-tuned Llama variant.
07:57 Priya Shah: yes we support bring-your-own-models in Private and Dedicated, and hosting in Redwood-hosted if license allows. version pinning and rollouts are supported.
08:08 Evan Cho: can we enforce that certain routes never call external tooling? like a DLP rule?
08:13 Priya Shah: yes, we have policies at routing layer and you can set function/tool-calling restrictions per route.
08:20 Jordan Blake: quick aside — i'll drop links to the security docs and the sample benchmark after the call.
08:26 Marta Ruiz: cool please include the evals we talked about.
08:29 Priya Shah: back to cost: the per-token table shows raw tokens, billed tokens, and effective cost after cache and batching. you can export and also set per-route budgets.
08:44 Evan Cho: can budgets cause circuit-breaker actions? like throttle or fallback to cheaper model?
08:49 Priya Shah: yes you can set budget policies that throttle or reroute to fallback variants; console has playbooks we can attach to alerts.
08:58 Marta Ruiz: in terms of SLA, what do you guarantee?
09:02 Jordan Blake: Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime; hosted has best-effort but we offer SLOs for enterprise customers. we'll include SLA info in follow-up.
09:12 Laura Kim: procurement needs an MSA template, do you share one?
09:16 Jordan Blake: yes, i'll send a standard MSA and we can iterate.
09:20 Marta Ruiz: what about granular cost per model version? if we push new finetune, can we compare cost/quality?
09:25 Priya Shah: yes — the console ties model versions to evals; you can compare quality metrics alongside cost and see regression alerts.
09:34 Evan Cho: show me the csv export.
09:37 Priya Shah: exporting now — here's a sample with route, tokens, billed_tokens, cache_hits, cost_usd. (typing) i'll attach the file to the follow-up.
09:50 Marta Ruiz: any gotchas for HIPAA?
09:53 Jordan Blake: HIPAA customers typically run Private, enable KMS, and set audit retention; we'll provide a compliance checklist.
10:03 Priya Shah: also note we have encryption at rest in all modes and role-based redact for sensitive fields in logs.
10:12 Evan Cho: fine, let's talk pilot timeline. we said 4/20?, 2 weeks to set up?
10:17 Jordan Blake: we'd propose kickoff 4/20, 2-week integration, 2-week benchmarking, then review.
10:23 Marta Ruiz: approved tentatively, need to align legal.
10:26 Laura Kim: procurement will review MSA and pilot credit details.
10:30 Jordan Blake: ok last bit — i'll send a tailored cost model showing your 100k monthly requests and two routes (patient-summary, triage) with hosted and dedicated comparisons.
10:40 Priya Shah: also dropping a short note on Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization per your traffic profile.
10:46 Marta Ruiz: awesome, grateful.
10:48 Jordan Blake: recap: we'll send pricing, security pack, sample dashboards, benchmark spreadsheet, and propose kickoff 4/20. any other questions?
10:56 Marta Ruiz: none for now, thanks.
11:00 Jordan Blake: thanks everyone, bye.
